title: Dengue with warning signs, 8-year-old girl
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Fever for 5 days, now abdominal pain and cold hands; less active than usual.
intake.history: Vomited three times today. Passed urine only once since the morning.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 1. A: Paediatric tables (MTS p12-18) apply (age 8, <12). Paediatric complaint pages 15-18 have their own header: x~131 = Level 1, x~244 = Level 2, x~358 = Level 3, x~453 = Level 4. DENGUE, SUSPECTED (p16) Level 1 cells: 'Fever onset 3 - 6 days' (day 5), 'Lethargy / Near-fainting' ('less active than usual'), 'Shock' (cold hands + CRT > 2 s + pulse pressure 14 mmHg + HR 128 + reduced urine = compensated shock by the dengue CPG definition). Paediatric primary triage CIRCULATION p13: 'Cold Peripheries' is Level 1 (x~137), 'CRT > 2 secs' is Level 2 (x~252). Paediatric vitals p14 (<12 years row; x~194 L1, 282 L2, 369 L3, 456 L4): SBP 90 sits on the 80-90 (L2) / 90-130 (L4) boundary, so L2 under the higher-modifier rule; HR 128 is in 120-150 = L3; RR 26 is in 25-40 = L3. Level 2 is acceptable if 'cold hands' is not taken as cold peripheries and shock is not called at triage; the L2 dengue cells (abdominal pain, persistent vomiting) apply regardless. B: Paediatric complaints list, 'Dengue, suspected' row (p16): Level 1 (x~131) is 'Fever onset 3 - 6 days', 'Lethargy / Near-fainting', 'Respiratory Distress', 'Shock'; Level 2 (x~244) is fever 3-6 days with abdominal pain or persistent vomiting. She is on day 5 and has compensated shock by the paediatric CPG criteria: cold extremities, CRT > 2 s, HR 128, pulse pressure 14 (<= 20), reduced urine output. That gives Level 1. The paediatric primary triage circulation row (p13) independently puts 'Cold Peripheries' at Level 1 (x~138-152) and 'CRT > 2 secs' at Level 2 (x~252-266). Paediatric vital signs for age < 12 years (p14): HR 128 is Level 3 ('120 - 150', x~370); SBP 90 falls on the boundary between the Level 2 cell '80 - 90 mmHg' (x~282) and the Level 4 cell '90 - 130 mmHg' (x~456); RR 26 is Level 3 ('25 - 40', x~370). Level 2 is acceptable if 'cold hands' is not read as cold peripheries and 'shock' is not recognised at triage.

disposition.note: Resuscitation in the ED critical zone first, then admission under paediatrics. The CPG mandates HDU/PICU only for prolonged or decompensated shock, so a monitored paediatric ward bed is also acceptable. HDU is preferred because of the required continuous ECG/SpO2, 15-30 minute perfusion checks and catheterised hourly urine output. Discharge is excluded (warning signs are an admission criterion). / Resuscitate in the ED red zone first, then admit under paediatrics. The CPG mandates HDU/PICU only for prolonged or decompensated shock. Compensated shock requires close monitoring by senior paediatric staff, which in practice is an HDU-level bed, so ADMIT_WARD (paediatric, closely monitored) is also acceptable.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Triage 1 vs 2 hinges on reading 'cold hands' as MTS paediatric 'Cold Peripheries' (Level 1) and on calling compensated shock at triage (dengue Level 1 'Shock' cell). CRT > 2 s alone is Level 2.
The 8-year-old falls in the MTS '< 12 years' vital-sign row (not '< 8 years'). SBP 90 is printed in both the L2 (80-90) and L4 (90-130) ranges.
Preferred disposition HDU vs monitored paediatric ward: the CPG does not require HDU for compensated shock.
The paediatric dengue CPG Table 1 cell text is interleaved in extraction; compensated-shock quotes are taken from the QR (p3) where the column text is contiguous.
B: The case title says 'dengue with warning signs', but the intake meets the paediatric CPG compensated-shock column: cold hands, CRT > 2 s, HR 128, pulse pressure 14, reduced urine output. I made compensated shock the primary diagnosis and 'warning signs' an acceptable alternative. The adjudicator may want to swap them.
Triage 1 rests on the 'Shock' and 'Cold Peripheries' Level 1 cells. The paediatric SBP of 90 sits on the boundary between the L2 cell '80 - 90' and the L4 cell '90 - 130'.
Preferred disposition HDU versus paediatric ward: the CPG wording supports 'closely monitored ... senior staffs' for compensated shock but names HDU/ICU only for prolonged or decompensated shock.
